title: Pig King’s Pet
paragraphs: “There’s a similar story in my world…”
“Like the Namahage… I think there was a similar variant with Santa Claus too.”

“The really scary ones are the ones called Mind Eaters or Magic Poisoners. Those capture you and directly drain your spirit, or they inject poison into your magic, rendering it unusable for a long time… sometimes even permanently. They also erode your consciousness.”
“Dangerous monsters exist everywhere.”
“Huh? I heard the Four Saint Heroes came from the Siltvelt side…”
Hearing the physician’s words, Father and the others look at me. What is it? If you stare at me like that, I’ll get embarrassed. Then, they quietly start checking the weapon inventory.
“There it is! I found it! I didn’t even notice we defeated it!”
“Dangerous! I didn’t know there was such a dangerous monster!”
“In the game, it was just a normal monster, but was it really that dangerous?”
“It’s not that strong.”
When I said that, the physician nodded. On the other hand, Father and the others seemed to be glaring at me for some reason.
“Well, its raw combat ability isn’t high.”
“Losing to it would be no joke.”
“In the game, I thought it gave a lot of experience for an enemy of the same level, but… so that’s the hidden truth behind it.”
“By the way, did you hunt them?”
“No, there were more efficient targets.”
Ren is finally answering honestly.
“Rato, are you currently researching ways to distinguish them?”
“Hmm, I was thinking about starting. Fortunately, another department seems to be working on it ahead of me, but it doesn’t seem to be going well.”
“That’s going to take time.”
“If it’s not something that can be resolved quickly, calming the chaos will be difficult.”
“The funding is there, so if the Four Saint Heroes cooperate, I think it could be done surprisingly fast.”
“Is it possible that the nobles are the ones funding it? Like, hoping their children aren’t invaders or something?”
“Half of it, yes. The other half is funding to prevent it… but that’s futile in the face of the Four Saint Heroes, isn’t it?”

There are various forces scheming behind the scenes in this world. From my perspective, I think this pig should just be taken out quickly. But considering what Father warned me about, I can’t completely dismiss his concerns, which is troubling. If someone told me to kill Sakura-chan because she was possessed by an evil spirit, I wouldn’t be able to go along with it. So, the physician and other alchemists are working on developing tools to distinguish between fakes and the real thing.
“Well, whatever. I think we can lend a hand in some way… but what should we do?”
“Hmm… Do the Four Saint Heroes know what I’m capable of?”
I raise my hand. I know why the physician is the physician, thanks to my knowledge from the first world.
“Alright, let’s start with the Spear Hero.”
“You can talk to the esteemed Filolials who can’t speak human language.”
“Ah… well, that’s not wrong. To be precise, it’s that you can communicate with monsters to some extent.”
“Windia can do that too, right?”
“Yeah. And if Gaelion is around, it’s not even necessary.”
“We don’t need three people for that.”
“Why am I being treated like a second-string and about to be laid off?”
The physician glares at us with half-open eyes.
“I just said I’m the same as Windia-chan.”
“I just meant that if Gaelion and the Filolials are around, there’s no need to talk to monsters. Windia is irrelevant.”
“I-I just reinforced the fact that we already have enough. The pace was too smooth, and it just slipped out.”
The physician opens the door at the back of the room and beckons Ren and Itsuki. In the back, the shadows of monsters are wriggling. Ren and Itsuki shake their heads furiously.
“Ahem! Anyway, I can communicate with monsters to some extent. That includes monsters that instinctively understand souls.”
“Oh!”
“Gaelion seemed to know too, but…”
“Didn’t he say he couldn’t tell the difference? Maybe we should ask the other kids?”
“…So that’s how it is.”
“But… for something that complicated, the monster’s intelligence and various other factors become necessary. Soul Vacuums aren’t very smart monsters, so they’re not helpful for reference.”
The physician answers with a sigh.
“So, what should we do then?”
“To create a tool or anything of the sort, we’d need a smart Soul Vacuum… Do you get what I’m saying? Four Saint Heroes who are raising a special Filolial and a dragon.”
Even Father and the others finally caught on to the physician’s provocation.
“If we use our hero skills to enhance the abilities of the Soul Vacuum and leave it with Rato, the research could progress faster?”
“That’s right. Could you talk to the castle and see if that’s possible?”
“Well, why not? It was all just a shot in the dark anyway.”
“Yeah, I think this is a clear and reasonable approach.”
“Indeed!”
Father thought about it for a moment but eventually nodded.
“Got it. I’ll talk to the people at the castle and see about getting a Soul Vacuum.”
“If possible, raise it from an infant. Once it becomes an adult, its intelligence doesn’t change much. A lot of people confuse it, but wisdom and intelligence are different, you know?”
“Understood. Well then… let’s get to it quickly.”
And so, we returned to the castle and placed an order for a Soul Vacuum. As a result, Father brought back a young Soul Vacuum from the castle, and we quickly leveled it up together.
“A glowing blue-white worm… right? It’s still pretty big after all.”
It’s a large worm, reaching about three meters in length. At night, it glows faintly.
“Nano~”
When Rival points, it obediently follows. It looks a lot like the monster called Dune that Father raised in the village.
“In the anime from Japan where I was, it looks like something that would be called a Nozuchi. It’s the kind of creature a yokai boy who shoots hair would probably keep as a pet.”
“Windia?”
“…Why did my name come up?”
It’s been a few days. Lately, I’ve had this restless feeling, like I’m forgetting something.
“A monster girl… that’s quite different, isn’t it?”
“Just thought it might be because of the vibe.”
The assistant glares at Ren, and Father asks.
“It seems true that it eats souls. It doesn’t eat any food we give it. But when it’s near the monsters we defeat, it feels like it’s absorbing something.”
“You could say there’s no waste…”
“It’s economical.”
“Naofumi, are you okay with it not costing anything?”
“But Gaelion-chan isn’t going to do something like living by feeding on the souls of defeated monsters, right?”
“If Naofuumi wants, I’ll do it nano! If it comes to that, Gaelion can even survive by eating mist nano!”
“I’m not sure how I feel about that…”
Father strokes the head of the Soul Vacuum. As expected, the response is good. Monsters kept as pets generally don’t dislike Father. Probably because he takes such good care of them.
“I’ve also recently gotten the hang of using the Soul Eater Spear effectively!”

Surprisingly, if I stab properly with this spear, I can extract only the soul from the prey. Well, it takes quite a bit of skill, so pulling it off smoothly is difficult. But I’ve managed to take out the soul without harming the body and use it as feed. The problem is that I can’t tell with just my eyes whether the soul has been extracted or not. I don’t have the ability to see spirits. Unless it’s a vengeful spirit-class entity, it’s hard to tell.
“For now, it’s grown to a decent size. According to Rato, it was raised from infancy, right?”
“It was a bit troublesome.”
“But bringing along a Soul Vacuum raised in the castle… that was something else.”

Now that I think about it, I remember seeing it when it was handed over. A large, swollen Soul Vacuum was reigning as the boss. It was supposedly a queen-class individual. If I had been careless, I might have crushed it with a single blow. By the way, it was the pet of the Pig King.
“When humans get involved, they grow that big. But… it didn’t seem like it was thinking much.”
I remember Rival trying to talk to it but giving up. I can’t understand monster conversations, but it seems difficult. In that regard, Filolials are much easier to understand. They’re so fluffy.
